texts: On day 470 of Year 2, the first snow of Year 2 fell in the early evening.
The snow was gone by dawn.
Every lantern burned normally that night.
The cold wind did not blow that night.
The mist-light was visible from a great distance, because the snow reflected the mist-light.
Coraline Ash counted many nightmoths at the Harbor Station that week.

q1_issues.issue: "the first snow **of Year 2**" drops the ordinal's stated restricting domain — `(Ordinal sk_snow_1 1 fall)` claims first-ever rather than first of that year (only partly recoverable from the fall event's own Year term).
"that week" is reduced to `(Time sk_count_1 (Year 2))`, so the anaphoric link to the day-470 week is not recorded; the conservative choice is right, but the week identity is lost.

q2_gaps: week-level temporal anchoring — the structured Time term vocabulary has Year / Month / Day / Weekday / Hour / Minute but no week term, so "that week" has no carrier under term propagation
a restricting domain on an `Ordinal` ("the first snow of Year 2") — the head has no slot for it and no entity-attached form is specified
review.notes: The rest is a close match to the instruction set: definite-projection out of the strength-0 denial, both reified-plus-flat copular dual-emits, precipitation and intransitive-subject roles, compound genus with an un-exposed noun modifier, and the name-with-kind-word handling of "Harbor Station". Treating `early_evening` as a decomposable compound kind rather than a bare day-part symbol is an extension, but a consistent one.

issues.reason: Core patterns states that a stated restriction is never silently dropped ('carry it, or leave the whole claim out and record the gap'), and no atom in the parse is traceable to the NP-internal 'of Year 2', so the bare (Ordinal sk_snow_1 1 fall) asserts rank 1 over snowfalls at large — more than the text states.

This mistakes a coverage gap for a parse defect: the Time term inventory (Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute) has no week term, so term propagation can only copy the antecedent's stated day-level terms, and (Time sk_count_1 (Year 2)) is true of the content and well-typed.

gaps_confirmed: no week-level Time term, so 'that week' has no carrier under anaphoric term propagation
a stated domain restriction on Ordinal — the head has no slot for it and no entity-attached carrier is specified
new_gaps: a day-of-year number ('day 470 of Year 2') has only the (Day <n>) term, which the instruction set exemplifies as day-of-month (June 5, 2021) and which the seeded same-year-month day-ordering rules read that way, so the two granularities are indistinguishable once stored
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is (Ordinal sk_snow_1 1 fall) beside an entity-attached restrictor carrying the stated Year-2 domain, in the AmongMost precedent's style ('one of the oldest orchards in the valley' keeps (In sk_orchard_1 sk_valley_1) on the entity); because no such carrier is licensed for a TEMPORAL domain — (Year 2) is a Time-family term and Time attaches to event witnesses, not to the snow substance witness — the only licensed form here is to drop the Ordinal claim entirely and record the gap rather than leave it unrestricted.
adjudication.notes: Everything else tracks the instruction set: definite typing projected out of the strength-0 wind denial, both reified-plus-flat copular dual-emits, the 'by dawn' TimeAtMost day-part bound, term propagation of day 470 / Year 2 / night onto the lantern rule and the wind denial, and the Kestrel-River handling of 'Harbor Station'. Decomposing early_evening as a compound day-part is improvisation, but every atom it emits is true and well-typed, so it is acceptable under the calibration line.
